Controls.ogVariedTip: What differs from orb to orb: how bouncy it is, how high it starts, when it is let go, its size, its gravity – or its period (perfectly elastic orbs that never settle).
Controls.ogDistributionTip: How the property spreads over the field: at random per orb (from the seed), corner to corner, centre outwards, by rows or columns, in a spiral, in ripple bands or as a checkerboard.
Controls.ogSpreadTip: How far the property ranges across the field. At 0 every orb is alike and the whole field bounces as one.
Controls.ogReleaseTip: When the orbs are let go: all together, ring by ring from the outside in or from the inside out, row by row, or in random slots.
Controls.ogStaggerTip: Seconds between two release steps (rings, rows or random slots).
Controls.ogDropHeightTip: How high the orbs start above the slab, in field widths.
Controls.ogOrbSizeTip: Orb diameter as a share of the spacing: at 100% neighbours touch.
Controls.ogBouncinessTip: How much of its speed an orb keeps at each landing (0.9 = 90%). A varied bounciness spreads around this value; 1 or more never settles.
Controls.ogResolveTip: Tunes every orb's timing a little (its bounciness stays) so that at one moment every moving orb lands at once – the pattern falls into phase, then dissolves again.
Controls.ogElevationTip: How far above the slab the camera looks down from, in degrees: low for a sweeping wave, 90° straight down.
Controls.ogRotationTip: Turns the field around its centre, in degrees.
Controls.ogOrbitTip: The camera slowly circles the field on the simulation clock, so a found run and its export look the same.
Controls.ogFloorTip: Under the orbs: a slab with a grid over a blue grid floor, a round dark plate, the grid alone, or nothing.
Controls.ogMaterialTip: Glossy (a bright highlight and a darker rim), chrome-like metallic, soft matte or see-through glass.
Controls.ogPaletteTip: Colours by current height (a rainbow from green to purple), by ring, by row, in the Ball Colour, or a rainbow by position.
Controls.ogHudTip: Shows the line “1089 bouncing orbs” at the top of the clip.
Controls.ogSoundTip: Notes: a soft tone per landing (a row or a ring lands as a chord). Sleep: very soft, long and low. Music: the landings compose a melody on your scale. Metal: bright clinks. Silent: nothing.
Controls.ogRunSettles: every orb at rest after about {seconds}s
Controls.ogRunNever: never settles – the clip ends the run
Controls.ogFull: Orbs in a run: {count} – the most one run holds ({requested} asked for).
Controls.ogPresetsTip: Fields after the most-liked orb clips: one click switches to Bouncing Orbs and loads the field, the look and the sound.
Controls.flDesc: Fighters from games, comics, shows and films duel in an arena with their weapons and one ability each. Pick a matchup or your own fighters. The last one standing wins.
Controls.flPresetTip: A ready-made matchup in its genre: it picks the fighters and the match type.
Controls.flMatchTip: A 1v1 duel, 2v2 (fighters A+B against C+D, no friendly fire), 3v3 (A+B+C against D+E+F), a free-for-all of three or four fighters, a bracket (entrants knocked out bout by bout until a champion) or a boss rush (the boss in slot A against challengers one at a time).
Controls.flFightersTip: Every slot's fighter, grouped by division. Random lets the seed pick one – Find Simulation then searches the matchup too.
Controls.flRandomHint: Picked by the seed from the whole roster.
Controls.flRandomHintDivision: Picked by the seed from the first fighter's division.
Controls.flSameDivisionTip: A random slot picks from the division of the first fighter chosen, so a matchup stays in its genre (comics vs comics, space saga vs space saga).
Controls.flHpTip: Every fighter's hit points (a fighter's row may give it a little more or less). Type any number from 1.
Controls.flTimeCapTip: After this many seconds the side with more HP left wins (equal HP is a draw). 0 = no cap: the fight goes on until a KO.
Controls.flArenaTip: A square or a circle, inset in the exported square under the names and above the ability boxes.
Controls.flHudTip: The names, the VS card, the ability boxes and the stat lines. Off: just the fight, its effects and the winner banner.
Controls.flHandicapsTip: Every fighter's multipliers of speed, damage, attack speed and cast speed (1 = as in the roster): rebalance a matchup or stage a buff – any number from 0.05.
Controls.lcDesc: Columns of blocks line the arena wall. A hit on a column takes its top block for the hitter's colour, and every eighth block adds a ball. The most blocks wins.
Controls.lcPresetTip: Load a ready-made battle: its rule, its wall, its competitors (a roster of countries) and the clip length.
Controls.lcRuleTip: What a hit on a column does to its top block.
Controls.lcHintKnock: The top block flies off in the hitter's colour and counts for it; a column knocked bare is just wall. The battle ends when every block is gone.
Controls.lcHintClaim: The top block stays where it is, painted in the hitter's colour; a column hands out its blocks from the top down. The battle ends when every block is claimed.
Controls.lcHintSteal: Like Claim, and a hit on a claimed column flips its top block that is not the hitter's – land sways back and forth until the duration runs out.
Controls.lcArenaTip: The shape of the wall the columns stand on.
Controls.lcTeamsTip: How many colours fight for the land – 2 to 12 on the slider, any number typed. The Teams roster names and colours the first ones (up to six), the palette the rest.
Controls.lcTeamsTipPyramid: How many colours knock the pyramid down: 1 to 12 on the slider, any number typed. One plays alone in yellow. The Teams roster names and colours the first ones, up to six, and the palette the rest.
Controls.lcpSoloNote: Played alone, in {name}. Two or more take the palette's colours, or set a roster in “Teams & Scoreboard”.
Controls.lcRosterNote: The first competitors ({count} of {teams}) take their colours, names and flags from the roster in “Teams & Scoreboard”; the rest come from the palette.
Controls.lcPaletteNote: Palette: {names}… – or set a roster in “Teams & Scoreboard” (its Country picker fills a team with a country).
Controls.lcBallsTip: The balls every competitor starts with.
Controls.lcColsTip: Columns of blocks round the wall, spread over its sides. Any number typed – columns finer than a pixel are drawn as one band.
Controls.lcRowsTip: How many blocks each column holds.
Controls.lcBlockCeiling: A run builds at most {max} blocks: {rows} per column with this many columns.
Controls.lcEveryTip: Every this many blocks a competitor takes add one more ball of its colour at the knock point (0 = never). Steals do not count.
Controls.lcDurationTip: The battle ends here at the latest (a steal battle always does); the clip length follows it.
Controls.lcTitleTip: The title line at the top of the HUD, drawn in capitals.
Controls.lcHudTip: The title, a live bar per competitor (its blocks and balls) and the counters at the top of the video. The verdict banner shows either way.
Controls.lcCaptionNote: A question caption whose answer – the winner – pops in at the verdict.
Controls.lcCaptionAdded: The question is in the Captions section; its answer [winner] names the winner.
Controls.lcRigNote: The Forced Winner is honest steering here: the chosen colour's balls rebound a little more towards land still to take, so it is the favourite, not a certainty. Find Simulation → Winner finds a run it wins.
Controls.teamCountryTip: Fill this team with a country: its name, its flag and its colour
Controls.sbHintCircle: STRING CIRCLE country fights: flag balls fan strings to the rim ahead of them, crossing a rival's strings cuts them, and the fans' share of the rim is the score.
Controls.scDesc: String Circle. Every ball anchors strings from itself to the rim ahead of it and drags a fan in its colour. Cutting through a rival's fan takes lives. The last flag standing wins.
Controls.scPresetTip: Fills the battle with a built-in country fight: its flags (the roster, from the Country picker's countries), the arena, the rates and a clip long enough for its battles.
Controls.scPresetCountries4: Battle of countries: Turkey / India / USA / Iran
Controls.scArenaTip: Circle: a thin white circle. Hexagon: the hexagon inscribed in it (the #hexagon clips). The fans reach whichever wall it is, and the rim arcs follow it.
Controls.scRateTip: How many strings every ball anchors a second, from itself to the rim straight ahead of it (any number from 1; the slider goes to 120). A fan's density is this times how long its strings last; a ball keeps at most 1,024 strings – past that its oldest fade out.
Controls.scCutTip: How many of a ball's strings its rivals must cut to take one of its lives (any number from 1). Nearly every string is cut sooner or later, so a battle lasts about lives × this ÷ (balls × strings per second).
Controls.scLineupNote: Balls past the roster play the line-up's countries, named by their codes: {codes}. A ball keeps up to {max} strings.
Controls.scRosterNote: Every ball wears the Teams & Scoreboard roster (its Country picker fills a row with a flag). A ball keeps up to {max} strings.
Controls.scTitleTip: The line at the top of the clip: empty shows STRING CIRCLE – type COUNTRY FIGHT or anything else (up to 40 characters).
Controls.scHudTip: A strip at the bottom of the clip: every flag still in with its share of the rim, the leader first (it takes the Teams scoreboard's place).
Controls.scCaptionAdded: The question is in the Captions section; its answer [winner] names the winning flag.
Controls.scCaptionNote: A question caption whose answer – the winning flag – appears when the last flag stands.
Controls.ogModelTip: Rhythm: every orb is an ideal bouncer – it keeps its height forever, so the field forms a smooth travelling wave that falls into phase at the end of every cycle, as in the clips. Decay: the orbs lose energy at every landing and come to rest.
Controls.ogRhythmTip: How many times each group bounces per cycle. Pendulum wave: 51, 52, 53 and so on. 3 against 2 up to 3:4:5: the voices meet on every downbeat. Euclidean: a ladder of tempos shared out evenly. Corner to corner and centre outwards: tempos rising across the field. Varied: a tempo per orb from the seed.
Controls.ogPolyTip: On: every group bounces a whole number of times per cycle, so the whole field lands together at the end of every cycle – IN PHASE – and morphs through waves in between. Off: one tempo for the whole field, its phase shifting across it – a steady travelling wave that never lines up.
Controls.ogGroupTip: How the field splits into groups that share a tempo: rows, columns, rings from the centre, diagonals from corner to corner, a checkerboard, or every orb on its own.
Controls.ogStepsTip: The Euclidean preset's ladder: this many neighbouring tempos, shared out among the groups as evenly as a Euclidean rhythm spreads its beats.
Controls.ogCycleTip: Seconds from one IN PHASE moment to the next: every orb lands together at its multiples. A longer cycle means slower bounces. With the metronome on, the cycle is a whole number of bars instead.
Controls.ogTempoSpreadTip: How far the tempos range across the field (corner to corner, centre outwards, varied): at 60% the fastest orbs bounce 1.6 times as often as the slowest. With Polyrhythm off: how far the phase shifts across the field.
Controls.ogEqTip: Every orb bounces to the same height. Off: an orb's height follows its period (apex = g·T²/8), so the faster bouncers bounce lower – as in the clips.
Controls.ogBounceHeightTip: The highest bounce – the slowest orbs', or every orb's with Equal Heights – in field widths at the default gravity; the Gravity slider scales it.
Controls.ogSquashTip: Each orb flattens by 10% when it lands and springs back over 60 ms.
Controls.ogMetroTip: Shows the beat in the clip: a pendulum bar swinging at the top, a ring pulsing around the field, or a dot hopping along a beat strip at the bottom. With the metronome on (or the click up) the cycle snaps to whole bars, so every IN PHASE moment lands on a downbeat.
Controls.ogBpmTip: The metronome's beats per minute. While the Sound section's beat lock is on, the metronome follows its tempo.
Controls.ogBeatsTip: Beats in a bar; the first one – the downbeat – is accented.
Controls.ogBarsTip: With the metronome on, the cycle lasts this many bars (16 bars at 120 BPM in 4/4 = 32 s), so the field is in phase on a downbeat.
Controls.ogClickTip: The metronome's woodblock click on every beat, accented on the downbeat; 0 = silent. Recorded with the clip.
Controls.ogMelodyTip: Every group plays its own note of the Sound section's scale – the slowest lowest – so the polyrhythm plays a tune: music composed by the bounces.
Controls.ogRunCount: {count, plural, one {# bounce} other {# bounces}} a cycle
Controls.ogRunNeverPhase: never in phase – one travelling wave
Controls.ogRunMetro: {bars, plural, one {# bar} other {# bars}} at {bpm} BPM
Controls.flSeekTip: How fast a fighter turns its flight toward the distance its weapon likes from its target (radians a second): swords and fists close in, shooters keep away, everyone strafes in range. 0 keeps the pure bounce of the first release – the fighters only bounce, and the walls nudge them toward a foe.
Controls.flSuddenDeathTip: At the time cap with two sides or more standing: up to 10 seconds of sudden death first, the arena shrinking to 60 % of its size (a knockout still ends it); then the side with the largest share of its HP left wins. Off: the HP share decides at the cap at once.
Controls.flSpectacleTip: How the fight looks – never what happens in it: the stage around the arena, the floor, the screen shake, the slow motion of the final knockout, impact frames, damage numbers, name tags and the plates of a 9:16 export.
Controls.flStageTip: The look around the arena: Noir (the default) a black stage with a thin white arena and white hit effects, Lilac a soft lilac backdrop with white ability cards, Night a dark backdrop, Theme the page's own theme. The fight is the same on every stage.
Controls.flArenaStyleTip: The arena's floor: Clean (plain), Grid, Division (each division's own rim colour and floor pattern – a match across divisions stays clean) or Neon (a glowing rim).
Controls.flShakeTip: How hard heavy hits, slams into the walls, bursts and knockouts shake the arena: 0 none, 0.6 by default, any number from 0 typed. With reduced motion on, the default is cut to 30 %; the camera's own Screen Shake replaces it while that is on.
Controls.flSlowMoTip: The final knockout plays a 1.2 s finale: slow motion, a push-in on the knockout and the winner's card 0.9 s in. Off: the card comes at once.
Controls.flImpactTip: Heavy hits (12 damage or more), giant hits and ability hits hold both fighters for a split second before they fly apart – only the drawing, never the fight.
Controls.flDmgNumbersTip: The numbers popping over the fighters: damage in colour tiers (a shotgun volley adds into one), heals and drains in green, giant hits in gold.
Controls.flPlatesTip: Only in 9:16 exports: the matchup in the bar above the arena and WHO WINS? – then the winner – in the bar below it.
Controls.flTagsTip: The short name under each ball: Auto with three or four fighters, On always, Off never.
Controls.flSoundGroupTip: How the fight sounds – never what happens in it: every fighter's own synthesized sound set, the match's stings and the announcer, or your own clips. Each applies live.
Controls.flSoundTip: Signature: every fighter's own synthesized set – its weapon, its ability, its division's colour. By weapon: the weapon kinds' and abilities' shared sounds. Classic: the first release's sounds.
Controls.flAnnouncerTip: The calls of the match – FIGHT!, first blood, KO, TIME!, the winner, PERFECT – as a deep synthetic voice and short stings, over the music.
Controls.flCustomSoundsTip: Plays the clips you added to a fighter's slots in place of its synthesized sounds. Off: the clips are kept but stay silent.
Controls.flClipPanelTip: Six slots for every fighter in the match: its attack, its hit, its ability, its KO, an optional intro and its win. A clip is at most 2 MB and plays its first 3 seconds.
Controls.flClipRightsNote: Add only audio you own or have a licence to use. Your clips stay on this device – they are never uploaded, never put in a link or a project file – and a video that uses them can still draw a content claim.
Controls.flClipTooLarge: That file is larger than 2 MB – pick a shorter clip.
Controls.flClipBadFile: That file is not an audio clip this page can play (WAV, OGG, FLAC, MP3, M4A or WebM).
Controls.flClipEmpty: Pick a fighter (not a random slot) to give it sounds of its own.
Controls.flClipImported: {count, plural, one {# clip imported} other {# clips imported}}
Controls.flClipImportBad: That file is not a fight sound set.
Controls.flClipOff: Custom sounds are off: the clips are kept but do not play.
Controls.growPresetsTip: One click sets the growth law, the fill, the colours and the look: Fill and loop (×1.11 a bounce from 5 %, a black page), Slow burn (4 % a bounce), Instant (60 % a bounce) or back to the classic Grow.
Controls.growLawTip: Approach: every bounce closes a share of the gap to the wall (the classic Grow, fast at first). Multiply: every bounce makes the ball a percentage bigger – slow at first, explosive at the end. Add: a fixed number of pixels a bounce. The new laws start small in the centre and bounce in clean chords.
Controls.growOnFillTip: Stay: the full ball keeps buzzing (the classic Grow). Loop: it holds, shrinks back to its start size and launches again – a seamless loop. Finish: the run ends at the fill, so Find Simulation can search it.
Controls.growStepTip: How much bigger the ball gets with every bounce: a percentage of its size (Multiply) or pixels (Add).
Controls.growStartTip: The ball's size at the start of every cycle, as a percentage of the ring.
Controls.growHoldTip: Seconds the full ball holds still (the completion chord rings) before it shrinks.
Controls.growShrinkTip: Seconds the ball takes to shrink back to its start size in the centre (eased); the next cycle starts when it is done.
Controls.growHueTip: The ball's colour follows its size along the colour stops below, from the first (small) to the last (full).
Controls.growRampTip: The colours the ball runs through as it grows (2 to 6 stops).
Controls.growMarkersTip: A small ring where the ball hits the wall, fading out (the last 64 are kept).
Controls.growMarkerLifeTip: Seconds a contact marker takes to fade out.
Controls.growPitchTip: Every bounce plays a soft pentatonic pluck that drops as the ball grows; the fill plays a completion chord and the shrink glides back up.
Controls.exportWholeLoopsTip: A looping run (Grow's Fill and loop) is recorded, fast-exported and batch-rendered as a whole number of its cycles, so the clip loops without a seam. Runs that do not loop are not affected.
Controls.loopHudTip: A bold lowercase title, an optional grey subtitle and one amber counter, drawn into every recorded frame (above and below the arena in a portrait clip).
Controls.loopHudTitleTip: The title line (shown lowercase); empty uses the mode's own words.
Controls.loopHudSubtitleTip: The grey line under the title; empty uses the mode's own words (none for most modes).
Controls.loopClipsTip: Load your own audio clip for a loop sound (a bounce, a bar, a chime, the completion…): it plays instead of the synthesis, live and in every recording and export.
Controls.loopClipsNote: Use only clips you have the rights to. They are decoded on this device and stay here – never uploaded, never shared, gone when you leave the page.
Controls.loopClipFailed: This file could not be decoded – try an MP3, WAV, OGG or M4A.
Controls.scStarDesc: Chord Stars. Every ball bounces round one circle at a fixed angle and draws a star polygon whose lines all touch one inner circle. Every star closes on the same frame with a chord, then the drawing fades and loops.
Controls.scStarPresetsTip: Five stars: five balls drawing 5/2, 7/3, 8/3, 9/4 and 12/5 from points spread round the rim. Seven-point bloom: seven heptagrams 7/3, each starting a seventh of a point further round. Heptagram duel: 7/2 against 7/3 from opposite sides. Each also sets the navy look and the loop HUD.
Controls.scBallsTip: How many balls draw a star, one star each (any whole number from 1; the slider goes to 12, a run builds at most 5,000). Balls past the typed stars take the next free ones.
Controls.scStarsTip: One star per ball as n/k: n points round the rim, the contact point moving k points with every bounce (5/2 is the pentagram). A step sharing a factor with n traces a smaller star several times (10/4 draws 5/2 twice); a step of 1 draws the plain polygon. Press Enter to apply.
Controls.scStarsRandomTip: A random coprime set for the balls: a different point count for each (5 and up, never 6), each with a random step that makes a real star.
Controls.scStarsExtended: Balls past the {typed, plural, one {# typed star} other {# typed stars}} draw the next free point counts, each with the step nearest 0.4 of it.
Controls.scCycleTip: Seconds every star takes to close (any number from 1; the slider goes to 30). Each ball moves at its own speed – its n chords in this time – so all of them close together.
Controls.scHoldTip: Seconds the closed drawing stays before it fades (0 starts the fade at once).
Controls.scFadeTip: Seconds the drawing takes to fade away before the next loop starts from the empty circle (0 cuts at once). One loop lasts drawing time + hold + fade.
Controls.scLoopNote: One loop lasts {loop} s and draws {chords} chords. Find Simulation picks a star set and fits the loop to the clip; Export whole loops keeps the clip seamless.
Controls.scSpreadTip: How far round the rim the balls' start points spread: 100% shares the whole rim out evenly, 0% starts every ball at the top.
Controls.scLineWidthTip: The width of the chords in px (any width from 0.5; the slider goes to 4).
Controls.scEnvelopeTip: The circle every chord of a star touches (radius R·cos(πk/n)): drawn as each star closes, all the time, or never.
Controls.scPaletteTip: Pastel: pink, cyan, yellow, green and lavender on navy (then more pastels). Rainbow: a hue for each ball. Ball color: every ball and its lines in the Ball Color.
Controls.scVoiceTip: Every bounce plays one note at its ball's own pitch – A major pentatonic, the slowest ball lowest: a soft pluck, a glass chime or a tuned bar. Silent leaves only the chord.
Controls.scChordTip: When every star closes: a warm open chord with a bell ding. When the drawing fades: a soft glide that lands under the next loop's first note, so the clip loops without a click.
Controls.hpPresetsTip: One click sets the hoops, the spin and the clip's look (the navy page, rainbow hoops, the title and the counter) and a clip of one whole cycle: eight rainbow hoops, one big hoop on a slow eased ramp, or two hoops climbing in two steps.
Controls.hpCountTip: How many concentric hoops spin together, one bead on each, evenly spaced from the outer to the inner radius. 1–16 on the slider; type any count (thousands are built).
Controls.hpRadiusMaxTip: The biggest hoop's radius as a share of the half field (the half field is one metre). A bigger hoop lifts its bead at a slower spin.
Controls.hpRadiusMinTip: The smallest hoop's radius as a share of the half field. A smaller hoop needs a faster spin before its bead climbs.
Controls.hpOmegaStartTip: The spin at the start of every cycle, in turns a second (0.13 in the clip). Below a hoop's critical spin its bead sits at the bottom.
Controls.hpOmegaEndTip: The spin the ramp reaches, in turns a second. Every hoop whose critical spin is below it lifts its bead, and a bead climbs higher the faster the spin.
Controls.hpCritical: The outer bead lifts past {outer} turns a second, the inner one past {inner}.
Controls.hpCriticalOne: The bead lifts past {outer} turns a second.
Controls.hpNeverLifts: {count, plural, one {# bead never lifts at this top spin.} other {# beads never lift at this top spin.}}
Controls.hpRampTip: Seconds the spin takes to climb from the start spin to the top spin. A slow ramp spaces the lifts out.
Controls.hpRampShapeTip: Linear climbs at a steady rate; Ease starts and ends gently; Steps climbs in as many equal steps as there are hoops – one bead a step.
Controls.hpHoldTip: Seconds at the top spin before the spin comes back down (or the run ends). It is stretched by less than a turn so every cycle holds whole turns.
Controls.hpReturnTip: Ramp the spin back down until every bead rests at its bottom again, then start over: a seamless loop (Export whole loops cuts the clip on the seam). Off: the run ends after the top hold.
Controls.hpReturnSecTip: Seconds the spin takes to come back down to the start spin; the beads drop back in reverse order.
Controls.hpGravityTip: Gravity pulling the beads down, in m/s² (9.81 on Earth). Stronger gravity raises every hoop's critical spin, √(g/R).
Controls.hpDampingTip: How quickly a bead's swing dies down, per second. 0 lets the beads swing around their balance points forever; more keeps them calm.
Controls.hpJitterTip: A tiny tilt of the spin axis in radians – the imperfection every real hoop has – to a side the seed picks, so the beads climb promptly to that side. At 0 a bead can balance on its bottom past the critical spin.
Controls.hpTickTip: A glock chime every turn, pitched higher as the spin climbs.
Controls.hpBedTip: A soft pad and sub on G that enters with the first lift and stops at the reset.
Controls.dpFanTip: Swing many double pendulums from one pivot, started a hair apart: they move as one line for a few seconds, then burst into a rainbow fan. The harp, sparring and the trail rest while it is on.
Controls.dpFanDesc: Every pendulum starts a tiny bit further round on its lower rod. The differences roughly double every fraction of a second, so the fan holds together for a few seconds and then suddenly splits.
Controls.dpFanPresetsTip: One click sets the fan, its rig, the clip's look (the navy page, the title, the subtitle and the state label) and a clip of one whole loop.
Controls.dpFanCountTip: How many double pendulums share the pivot. Any number from 1 can be typed; at most 5,000 are built (what one step's budget integrates).
Controls.dpSpreadDegTip: The total difference in the lower rod's start angle across the whole fan, in degrees. At 0 every pendulum stays identical for ever; a bigger spread splits the fan sooner.
Controls.dpColourByTip: Rainbow by index: each pendulum takes its own hue as it leaves the leader (white lines and a pink bob while they are still one). One colour: every pendulum in the Ball Color.
Controls.dpPalindromeTip: Record the forward run, then play it backwards, so every pendulum retraces its path home and the clip loops seamlessly.
Controls.dpFanLoopLine: A loop of {cycle}s: {forward}s forwards, then the same film backwards.
Controls.dpFanForwardOnly: The fan only runs forwards: the run ends at the clip length.
Controls.dpForwardSecTip: Seconds the fan runs forwards before it plays back. The loop lasts twice as long.
Controls.dpDivergePxTip: The fan counts as split once a bob is this far from the leader's bob (pixels on a 1080-pixel-wide video). It times the split cue, the colours and Find Simulation's split.
Controls.prSpiralDesc: Phase spiral. Give every ring several dots and they wind into a spiral, pass through interference patterns and straighten into spokes once a cycle. The in-line meter counts toward it.
Controls.prSpiralPresetTip: The loop clip in one click: 20 rings with 3 arms each, a 20 s loop that never ends, the in-line meter, comet tails, the loop sounds and the spiral colours on a navy page with the loop HUD.
Controls.prArmsTip: Dots on every ring (Rings and Spiral layouts), evenly spaced. A dot steps one spoke a tick, so the rhythm stays the same while the picture becomes a spiral with that many arms that straightens into its spokes once a cycle. Any whole number from 1 can be typed.
Controls.prAlignMeterTip: Shows "in line N%" over a thin bar: how close the dots are to lining up on their spokes – 100% at every alignment, near 0 in between. Under the disc, or as the loop HUD's counter while the HUD is on.
Controls.prTrailTip: How far a dot's tail reaches back, in seconds of its motion (0 = no tail). Longer tails draw the arms of the spiral.
Controls.prLoopSoundTip: Original synthesized loop voices instead of the instrument: a pentatonic pluck on every tick (inner rings low, outer rings high), risers as the meter passes 50, 75 and 90%, and an open chord with a bell on every alignment.
Controls.prPaletteTip: Rainbow round the colour wheel, or the spiral look: blue and cyan inside, through green and yellow to orange and red outside, on a dark disc.
Controls.efDesc: An elliptical pool. A volley of balls fires from one focus, bounces off the wall and passes through the other focus all at once. Every pass lands on the beat.
Controls.efPresetTip: Starting points: the clip's whispering gallery, one billiard shot with its path, a thousand-ball volley, the circle control and a 90° fan. A preset sets the mode's own settings and its look.
Controls.efCountTip: Balls fired at once from the start focus, spread evenly over the spread angle. Any whole number can be typed; a run builds at most the engine's ball ceiling.
Controls.efEccentricityTip: How stretched the pool is: 0 is a circle (both foci at the centre, every ball back there), 0.99 a long thin pool. The clip uses 0.65.
Controls.efFlatNote: An eccentricity of 1 or more has no inside: the run uses {max}.
Controls.efSizeTip: The pool's long semi-axis as a share of the safe radius (100% fills the recorder's centred square like the ring modes' arena).
Controls.efTransitTip: Seconds a ball takes from one focus to the wall and on to the other focus. Every path is 2a long, so the speed is 2a / T and every volley converges exactly T later. Set whole bars of a tempo (T = bars × 4 × 60 / BPM) and the convergences land on the beat.
Controls.efPassesTip: Transits in a loop: with Refire a fresh volley leaves the start focus every this many passes and the clip loops seamlessly (loop length = passes × T).
Controls.efLoopNote: A convergence every {transit} s (the groove at {bpm} BPM: two bars a pass) – the loop is {loop} s.
Controls.efLoopNoteCollapse: A convergence every {transit} s (the groove at {bpm} BPM) – no loop: the swarm keeps collapsing onto the long axis.
Controls.efSpreadTip: The volley's spread: 360° fires every way, less fires a fan centred on the other focus.
Controls.efAimTip: Turns the whole volley (0° fires one ball straight at the other focus and keeps the volley mirror-symmetric). Find Simulation's Longest collapse searches it.
Controls.efLaunchTip: The focus the volley is fired from: the top or the bottom one (left or right when the pool lies down).
Controls.efOrientationTip: The pool's long axis: standing up (vertical, the clip) or lying down (horizontal).
Controls.efResetTip: What happens when the swarm converges: refire a fresh volley from the start focus every Passes per loop (the seamless loop), let it keep collapsing, or refire a fresh volley at every pass.
Controls.efResetRefireHint: A fresh volley leaves the start focus every loop, under the convergence's flash – the loop is seamless.
Controls.efResetCollapseHint: One volley for the whole run: every pass narrows it until it slides along the long axis as a tight comet.
Controls.efResetEveryHint: A fresh volley at every convergence, from the focus the swarm landed on: the arc never collapses.
Controls.efSkinTip: The pool's look: a pool table (wooden rim, copper rail, green felt), a neon outline in the Wall Color, or a thin line.
Controls.efTrailTip: Seconds of flight each ball's comet trail shows, tapering and fading to nothing (0 = no trails).
Controls.efPathsTip: Draws every ball's chords since its volley faintly over the felt (within the Lines mode's stroke budget: a big volley shows its newest corners).
Controls.efBedTip: A soft pad, a sub and a kick on every beat at 8 · 60 / T BPM under the plucks, changing chord every pass – a convergence always lands on a bar line.
Controls.efCounterTip: Shows the passes of the current loop under the pool in the Loop HUD (“3 passes”; the clip has none). Turning it on turns the Loop HUD on.
Controls.flPresetGalleryTip: Ready-made matchups by format – duels, best-of-3 rivalries, team fights, free-for-alls, brackets, boss rushes and reworks (a buffed or nerfed fighter) – every one inside one division (a bracket inside one genre).
Controls.flSurpriseTip: Picks a division and two of its fighters for a duel.
Controls.flShowsTip: A best-of series, a bracket or a boss rush plays as one run: every match with its VS card, then a short card between matches. The recording and Find Simulation follow the whole show.
Controls.flBestOfTip: A series on 1v1, 2v2 and 3v3 (and a bracket's final): the first to win more than half the games wins. A draw or a double KO counts for nobody and the game is played again; after n + 2 games the higher HP share decides. An even number rounds up (Bo4 plays as Bo5); 1 = one match.
Controls.flEntrantsTip: Comma-separated fighter ids and tokens: random, random:<division or genre>, division:<id> (the whole division in roster order). Empty: the format's own pool – the division of fighter A (a boss rush: the boss's, Comics A for Gerald). Unknown names are dropped.
Controls.flBracketSizeTip: Entrants of the bracket, from 2 (no maximum; a run builds at most 256). A size that is not a power of two gives byes to the top seeds. Each bout is a duel with a time cap of at most 45 s and sudden death; Best Of applies to the final only.
Controls.flSeedingTip: By rating (the simulated strength of the balance tuner), by the seed, or in the order listed (pinned slots first). The top seeds meet only in the final.
Controls.flBossWavesTip: How many challengers face the boss, one at a time, from 1 (no maximum; a run builds at most 256).
Controls.flBossHpTip: The boss's HP multiplier (from 0.05, no maximum). The boss is also 1.5× the size and deals 1.25× the damage, keeps its HP between bouts and enters PHASE 2 (faster, quicker casts) at half its HP.
Controls.flBossHealTip: The share of its maximum HP the boss heals between two bouts (from 0, no maximum).
Controls.flCardSecTip: Seconds of the card between two matches of a show – the score, the bracket or the boss's status (from 0, no maximum).
Controls.flOddsTip: The VS card shows each side's win chance, simulated from the balance tuner's ratings ('est.' where no rating measures the pairing). Hidden whenever a handicap is set: BUFFED and NERFED tags show instead.
Controls.flPinnedHint: Slots A–F pin entrants (seeds 1–6 when listed); a random slot pins nothing. Find Simulation and the forced winner pick among the pinned entrants.
Controls.flBossPinnedHint: Slot A is the boss (Gerald when random); slots B–F pin the first challengers.
Controls.flCreatorTip: Turn the current matchup into a ready-made clip, or download a tier list card of a division or a genre.
Controls.flMakeClipTip: Searches a seed of the current matchup and format whose story fits the clip. A single match is paced so its final KO lands near the end. A cliffhanger is cut while every fighter is low. A series, bracket or boss rush ends with its verdict. The clip length, a caption and the Top Text are set for you.
Controls.flClipSearching: Searching for the story – the progress shows in the Find Simulation strip.
Controls.flClipFound: Clip ready: {sec} s with the final KO at {pct} % – press Start or record it.
Controls.flClipFoundCut: Clip ready: {sec} s, cut while every fighter is low – the question stays open.
Controls.flClipMissed: No seed told this story – try another story, length or matchup.
Controls.flTierListTip: A card of a division or a genre ranked S–D by every fighter's win share in the simulated round robin (top 15 % S, next 20 % A, middle 30 % B, next 20 % C, bottom 15 % D), downloaded as a PNG for a feed post (1080×1350) or a story (1080×1920).
Controls.flTierDisclaimer: Names are plain text labels of an unaffiliated fan simulation – no logos, artwork or audio.
Controls.lcLayoutTip: Wall: the columns line the arena's wall (the battles). Pyramid: a stepped pyramid of columns stands in the middle of a floor, shown in 3D, and the balls knock it down block by block – the summit last.
Controls.lcpDesc: Every ball that hits a column knocks its top block off. Every eighth block knocked off adds another ball. The outer steps fall first and the summit last.
Controls.lcPyramidSizeTip: Columns along each side of the pyramid's base (11 makes an 11 × 11 grid). Any number from 3 can be typed.
Controls.lcStepsTip: The steps of the pyramid: a column is as tall as the steps minus its distance from the centre, so the summit is the tallest and the outer ring the lowest.
Controls.lcBlocksTip: The blocks in all: the steps are scaled so the pyramid holds exactly this many (1,144 by default). 0 keeps the steps' own count.
Controls.lcpBlocksNatural: natural: {count, plural, one {# block} other {# blocks}}
Controls.lcpSummary: {blocks, plural, one {# block} other {# blocks}}, the summit {tallest, plural, one {# block} other {# blocks}} high – {balls, plural, one {# ball} other {# balls}} when the last one falls.
Controls.lcRebuildTip: When the last block falls the pyramid builds itself again and the run starts over from its first frame, so a clip of whole cycles loops forever (Export whole loops in the Recording section).
Controls.lcRebuildSecTip: Seconds the rebuild takes: the columns rise back from the floor, the added balls melt into the pyramid and the first ones glide back to their corners.
Controls.lcpLoopNote: The run loops: knocked down, a short hold, rebuilt, and the first frame again. Find Simulation searches the first cycle; the clip covers a whole one.
Controls.lcpEndNote: The run ends when the last block falls (or at the battle duration), like a battle on the wall.
Controls.reDesc: Ring Escape, after the loop family's oldest reel: lay the gaps out in a spiral, turn the rings together, paint them in a rainbow, time every ring and hear a rising note for each ring the ball gets through.
Controls.reSpiralPresetTip: The reel's look: a pure black page, eleven thin rainbow rings whose gaps step round in a spiral and turn together, a white ball with a short trail and the ring sounds. No title and no counter.
Controls.gapLayoutTip: Where each ring's gap starts. Even: spread evenly round the rings (the classic look). Random: anywhere, drawn from the run's seed. Aligned: every gap in one straight line. Spiral: each gap a fixed step round from the one inside it.
Controls.gapSpiralStepTip: Degrees between the gaps of neighbouring rings in the spiral layout. 0 lines them all up; the field takes any value from 0.
Controls.ringSpinTip: Alternate: neighbouring rings turn opposite ways (the classic rings). Together: every ring turns the same way at the same speed, so a spiral stays a spiral while it turns.
Controls.ringRainbowTip: Colours each ring by its place: red outside, through orange, yellow and green, to cyan inside.
Controls.ringTimerTip: Shows "ring k: t s" under the rings: how long the ball has been in the ring it is in, and "out in t s" once it is out. Recordings carry it.
Controls.ringSoundTip: Original synthesized sounds: a soft pentatonic pluck for every bounce, pitched by the ring (outer rings low, inner rings high), a rising step for every ring the ball gets through and a warm chord when it is out.
Controls.sbLifeTip: Strings keeps a ball alive while one of its threads holds, and Lives gives every ball a set number of lives.
Controls.sbLifeHintStrings: A ball lives while one of its threads holds. Lose the last one and it shatters.
Controls.sbLifeHintLives: Every ball starts with a set number of lives. A lost life shields it for a moment.
Controls.sbHintCutStrings: Crossing enemy threads cuts every one you pass. Bounce often to grow new ones.
Controls.sbHintTouchStrings: The threads are lasers. Touching one costs you your oldest thread.
Controls.sbHintCollideStrings: Every crash costs the slower ball its oldest thread.
Controls.sbDuelTip: When two balls are left they hunt each other, every cut slows time, and a heartbeat builds to the end.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: One ball, a stack of rings, one gap each. Every ring it slips through breaks. Will it get out?

accumulation.name: Accumulation
accumulation.description: Escape in time or freeze in place. Every frozen ball blocks the next one. The arena fills fast.

multiply.name: Multiply
multiply.description: Every escape spawns more balls. One ball becomes a swarm in seconds.

lines.name: Lines
lines.description: A line from the ball to every bounce. The run draws its own string art.

paint.name: Paint
paint.description: The ball paints a rainbow trail and a counter climbs to 100%. Can it cover the whole circle?

target.name: Target
target.description: Numbered targets on the wall. Hit them in order and each one breaks. Miss and it flashes red.

grow.name: Grow
grow.description: The ball grows with every bounce until it fills the ring and has nowhere left to go.

shatter.name: Shatter
shatter.description: Every wall is made of cracked segments. Each hit chips one off. Smash a path out.

colorMatch.name: Color Match
colorMatch.description: The ball changes colour on every bounce. A segment breaks only when the colours match.

portal.name: Portal
portal.description: Touch a portal and the ball jumps to its twin. After a few trips the portals burn out and open.

drop.name: Ball Drop
drop.description: Balls of every size rain through a pegboard. Every hit is a note. Big balls low, small balls high.

box.name: Bouncing Shapes
box.description: Squares and logos glide round a box and count down with every bounce. A corner hit is the accent.

pendulum.name: Pendulum Wave
pendulum.description: Pendulums drift out of line, split into waves and snap back together every cycle. Every crossing is a note.

polyrhythm.name: Metronomes & Polyrhythms
polyrhythm.description: Hundreds of voices tick at their own tempo and drift apart. Then they all hit at once with a flash.

collide.name: Collision Playground
collide.description: Hundreds of orbs bump round a circle. Every collision is a soft note, pitched by size.

glass.name: Glass Smash
glass.description: Gerald drops through floors of glass. Every landing cracks a pane and plays a note. The last hit shatters it.

multipliers.name: Multipliers
multipliers.description: Balls fall through gates that clone them. A handful becomes hundreds on the way home. A counter keeps score.

doublePendulum.name: Double Pendulum Harp
doublePendulum.description: A chaotic double pendulum swings over a harp. Every string it crosses plays a note.

illusion.name: Circle Illusion
illusion.description: Balls on straight lines that secretly roll a circle, rings that ripple, a picture hidden in the paint.

stringBattle.name: String Battle
stringBattle.description: Every bounce leaves a glowing thread. Cut an enemy thread and they lose a life. Last ball standing wins.

powerLayers.name: Power Layers
powerLayers.description: A ball bounces against a stack of hundreds of rainbow layers. Every hit destroys more. The power doubles.

race.name: Square Racing Grand Prix
race.description: Squares race down a track of bumpers, funnels and turbo pads. Live standings, a podium, confetti.

battle.name: Square Battle Royale
battle.description: Up to twenty squares with health bars crash into each other. Last square standing wins.

ctf.name: Capture the Flag
ctf.description: Two teams of squares, a flag at each end. Grab the enemy flag and get it home to score.

runner.name: Beat Runner
runner.description: A square runs and jumps to the beat of your song. Every landing hits a beat and plays a note.

paddle.name: Paddle Keep-Up
paddle.description: Keep the ball up with a sliding platform. Every catch is a note. Miss too often and it is over.

vortex.name: Sound Vortex
vortex.description: Balls spiral down a whirlpool of sound rings. Every ring is a note. The hole swallows them with a pew.

journey.name: Journey
journey.description: Gerald bounces through his commute. Rings, glass, pegs and gates, stage after stage, all the way home.

bullseye.name: Bullseye
bullseye.description: Balls fire through pegs onto a dartboard. Every ring scores. A centre hit is a bullseye with confetti.

mergeRing.name: Merge Ring
mergeRing.description: Balls drop into a rainbow ring and fuse tier by tier. Does the final form appear before it overflows?

spiralGlass.name: Spiral Glass
spiralGlass.description: Balls circle a glass spiral and chip it away from the outside in. Every lap adds a ball. Will it multiply?

beatDrop.name: Beat Drop
beatDrop.description: Platforms fly in just before each beat, so every landing hits the beat. Made for music edits.

territory.name: Territory
territory.description: Two or four teams of balls paint a tile map their colour. One bounce can flip the board.

maze.name: Maze Escape
maze.description: Balls drop into a glowing maze and bounce their way out, painting every corridor red. First one out wins.

conveyor.name: Conveyor Belt
conveyor.description: A belt drops a new ball into the arena every few seconds. The pile grows and the counter keeps score.

orbGrid.name: Bouncing Orbs
orbGrid.description: Thousands of orbs bounce on their own spot. Waves roll across the field until every orb lands together.

fightLeague.name: Fight League
fightLeague.description: Fighters from games, comics and films duel as balls with their own weapons. Last one standing wins.

landClaim.name: Land Claim
landClaim.description: Columns of blocks ring the arena. Balls knock them off for their colour. Most blocks wins.

starChords.name: Chord Stars
starChords.description: Balls draw star polygons inside one circle. Every star closes on the same frame with a chord.

hoops.name: Spinning Hoops
hoops.description: Hoops spin faster and faster. One by one the beads climb, biggest hoop first, each with its own note.

colourSort.name: Colour Sort
colourSort.description: Mixed balls sort themselves through one-way gates into a bullseye of colours, then mix again.

ellipseFoci.name: Focus Shot
ellipseFoci.description: A volley of balls fires from one focus and lands on the other all at once, pass after pass.

beatMachine.name: Beat Machines
beatMachine.description: Marbles drop onto tuned bars or a ball hops down a staircase. Every note lands right on the beat.

waveTank.name: Wave Tank
waveTank.description: Waves squeeze through one, two, then seven gaps and cross into stripes. A row of bells plays the water.

brickRebuild.name: Brick Smash
brickRebuild.description: A picture made of bricks gets smashed by balls that multiply. Then it rebuilds, colour by colour.

drawingMachine.name: Drawing Machines
drawingMachine.description: Three pendulums swing one pen across paper, or Earth and Venus draw a five-petal flower.

perfectFit.name: Perfect Fit
perfectFit.description: Pieces drop straight down into a box until it is exactly full. Not one square is left over.

q1.question: Is {siteName} free to use?
q1.answer: Yes. Every mode, every setting and recording are free, with no account. Free videos carry a small watermark, and Pro removes it for {monthly} a month or {yearly} a year.

q2.question: What video formats and sizes can I export?
q2.answer: Square 500×500, HD 1280×720, Full HD 1920×1080 and vertical 1080×1920, from 10 to 120 seconds. Chrome and Safari export MP4. Firefox exports WebM.

q3.question: Can I use the videos commercially?
q3.answer: Yes. Everything you make is yours to post anywhere, with no credit needed. The names of characters in Fight League belong to their owners.

q4.question: Do I need to install anything?
q4.answer: No. It runs in your browser. Open the site and start.

q5.question: Can I save my settings?
q5.answer: Yes. Save presets in your browser and load them any time. The link in the address bar also carries your setup, so you can bookmark or share it.

q6.question: Does it work on mobile?
q6.answer: It runs on phones, but it is built for a laptop or desktop, where the canvas and the controls fit side by side.

q7.question: Are there keyboard shortcuts?
q7.answer: Yes. Space pauses and resumes. R restarts.

q8.question: How do I put my own image on the ball?
q8.answer: Open Ball & Physics, turn on Show Advanced Options and click Choose Image. Any image works, or pick an emoji.

q9.question: Can the bounces play music?
q9.answer: Yes. In Custom Sound pick a song from the library or import a MIDI file, and every hit plays the next note. Or switch to an audio sample, built in or your own.

Editorial.tipFindSimulationBody: Set the clip length you want and let Find Simulation scan seeds for a run that lasts exactly that long. Then record it.
Editorial.tipTextHooksBody: A line at the top like “Will it escape?” gives viewers a reason to stay. Keep it big enough to read on a phone.
Editorial.tipClipLengthBody: Short clips of 15 to 30 seconds are a good start. Set the length in Recording and pick 1080×1920.
Editorial.tipSpeedBody: Use 2× to 8× to skip through a long run while you set it up. Go back to 1× before you record.
Editorial.troubleExportQ: The video export looks wrong or is missing frames
Editorial.troubleExportA: Use a recent Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Close other tabs and keep this tab visible while it records. Firefox exports WebM, which every platform accepts.
Editorial.troubleAudioA: Browsers block sound until you click the page. Click anywhere, then press Start. If it is still silent, check the system volume and the site’s sound permission.
Editorial.troubleSpeedQ: The ball moves too fast or too slow
Editorial.troubleSpeedA: Open Ball & Physics and change Ball Speed. Lower gravity keeps the ball floating longer between hits.
Editorial.troubleSettingsA: Presets live in your browser's storage. A private window or clearing site data removes them. Copy the share link of a setup you want to keep.
Editorial.troubleMidiQ: My MIDI file does not load
Editorial.troubleMidiA: Very complex files may not parse. Try a single-melody MIDI. The tool keeps only the highest note at each moment.
Editorial.troubleStuckA: Send a note through the feedback page and tell us what you were doing.

Privacy.metaDescription: How {siteName} handles your data. What stays in your browser, what is sent when you publish or pay, and the storage the site uses.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.content: Welcome to {siteDomain} ("we", "our", "us"). We respect your privacy and keep the amount of information connected to your use of this site as small as possible. This policy covers the website and the Windows app. It explains what is collected, how it is used and what your rights are.

information.title: Information We Collect
information.subtitle: We collect the minimum needed to run and improve the service:

analytics.label: Visit statistics:
analytics.content: On the website we count visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics. It reports the page that was opened, the site you came from, your country, your device type, your browser and your operating system. Cloudflare says it uses no cookies or local storage for this and does not fingerprint visitors.

localStorage.label: Local storage data:
localStorage.content: Your settings and presets are stored in your browser's local storage on your device and are not sent to our servers. The same place holds your Pro licence and, if you use them, your account sign-in and publishing connections. Those go only to the service they belong to, as described below.

images.label: Uploaded images and audio:
images.content: Custom ball images, MIDI files and sound clips are processed entirely in your browser. They are not uploaded. A clip you make with them leaves your device only if you publish it.

events.label: Action counts:
events.content: We also count a few actions, such as starting the simulator, exporting a clip or opening the checkout, with a statistics service at {host}. It records the address of the page, including any campaign name or ad click identifier in it, the site you came from, your browser, your screen size and your country. In the studio that address also holds the settings of your run, so the service can see them. It never receives your email or your receipt reference. It does not run if your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, and it does not run in the Windows app.
events.optOut: Turn the action counts off in this browser.
events.optedOut: Action counts are off in this browser.

account.label: Account data:
account.content: If you create an account, the relay server keeps your email address, the name you gave and a salted hash of your password. See Publishing below.

payment.label: Payment data:
payment.content: If you buy Pro, our billing server keeps your email, the plan and the payment provider's reference. See Payments below.

howWeUse.title: How We Use Your Information
howWeUse.content: Visit statistics show us how the site is used so that we can improve it. Your email and the payment reference are used to issue, renew and restore your Pro licence. We do not sell your data and we do not share it with advertising networks.

legalBases.title: Why we may process your data
legalBases.content: We process data on these legal grounds. To run the site, the relay and the Windows app and to answer you: our legitimate interest in running the service, and the contract with you once you buy Pro or create an account. To issue, renew and restore your licence and to keep payment records: the contract and the tax and accounting laws that bind us. To count visits and a few actions: our legitimate interest in knowing how the site is used, with no cookies and an opt out through Do Not Track, Global Privacy Control or the switch above. To send a clip to a platform or to Postiz: your request, each time you press send or approve. Nothing is processed on the basis of consent except where we ask for it.

cookies.title: Cookies and Tracking
cookies.content: This site sets no cookies. Your language is part of the page address, and your settings stay in your browser's local storage. The payment pages of Stripe and NOWPayments, and the sign-in pages of TikTok, Instagram and Google, belong to those companies and may set their own cookies.

thirdParty.intro: These companies handle data for us or for you. Each does so under its own privacy policy.

transfers.title: Where your data goes
transfers.content: Cloudflare, Stripe, GitHub, Hugging Face and Google are based in the United States and may process data there. Each one is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and its UK extension, or works under the EU standard contractual clauses and their UK addendum, which keep EU and UK protection in place. Postiz and any cloud AI provider you choose are your own providers, and their location is in their own policies.

retention.title: Data Retention
retention.content: Local storage data stays on your device until you clear it. The billing server keeps your email, the plan and the provider's reference for as long as your licence can be restored and for 10 years after the last payment, the longest accounting retention period that can apply to us. Then it is deleted. Webhook records are deleted after 30 days. An account on the relay is kept until you delete it on the Account page. Its session tokens expire after 30 days. A clip uploaded to the relay is deleted after 24 hours. Visit statistics are kept by the services that produce them under their own rules.

children.title: Children's Privacy
children.content: The service is not directed at children under 13. You must be at least 16 to create an account and 18 to buy Pro. If we learn that we hold data of a child under 16, we delete it. Parents can write to us at the address above.

An upload to YouTube goes from your browser straight to Google, with an access token kept in your browser's local storage. Removing the account in the block deletes the token. Uploads to TikTok and Instagram, and to YouTube if you choose, go through a relay server. You sign in to it with an access key from whoever runs it, or with an account you create on the Account page.

TikTokBallVideos.title: Bouncing Ball Videos for TikTok
TikTokBallVideos.p1: Bouncing-ball videos are easy to follow. A ball trapped in rings tries to bounce its way out, and people stay to see if it does. {siteName} is built for exactly these clips, free, with a vertical export. Pro removes the watermark.
TikTokBallVideos.p2: The tension is built in. The ball speeds up, the gap looks too small, then it slips through and the wall breaks. That fits in a clip of 15 to 60 seconds.
TikTokBallVideos.p3: A ball that might escape gives people a reason to watch to the end, and to watch again. Add a melody and every wall hit plays the next note.
TikTokBallVideos.p4: No dialogue, no face, no setup. A clean visual hook that works even for someone half-scrolling.
TikTokBallVideos.p5: TikTok wants 9:16 vertical, 1080×1920. {siteName} records at that size, so there is no cropping and no editor. Set the length, press record, download.
TikTokBallVideos.p6: You can also export square, HD or Full HD for Reels, Shorts and other platforms. Recording happens in your browser and nothing is uploaded. Free videos carry a small {siteName} watermark. Pro removes it.
TikTokBallVideos.p7: A clear hook in the first second, a visible counter, and a payoff when the ball escapes. Find Simulation picks a seed for the clip length you want, so you plan instead of guessing.
TikTokBallVideos.p8: Every mode has its own rhythm, from Classic to Glass Smash. Save your favourite setups as presets and post a new video every day.

About.metaTitle: About {siteName}, the Ball Physics Video Maker
About.metaDescription: Why {siteName} exists. A browser tool for making bouncing-ball videos for TikTok, Reels and Shorts. Free to play and export.
About.metaOgDescription: Why {siteName} exists and who it is for.
About.title: About {siteName}
About.p1: {siteName} started with a simple problem. Bouncing-ball videos were everywhere, and every way to make one was slow. Learn a game engine, pay for an app, or repost someone else's clip. We wanted to open a tab, make the video and post it. So we built that.
About.p2: {siteName} is free and runs in your browser. No sign-up, no install. Every mode and setting is yours to play with, and so is the export. Free videos carry a small watermark. Pro removes it.
About.p3: Speed and control. Speed, because a clip that takes twenty minutes and three apps never gets made. Control, because a video you shaped yourself stands out in a feed full of reposts.
About.p4: We also stay out of your way. The simulator updates as you change things, so you learn by doing. Settings have plain names.
About.p5: Your work stays with you. Presets live in your browser and videos render on your own machine. We do not want your data. The details are in our <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.text: We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. The simulator respects reduced motion and the pages work with a keyboard. Tell us through the feedback page if something is in your way.

About.p6: {siteName} is a small independent project. New modes and settings appear because creators ask for them. Write in through the <feedback>feedback page</feedback>.
About.p7: The core stays free. More modes, more effects, fewer steps between an idea and a posted clip. Go make a ball smash through some walls.
About.toolP1: A browser tool for the bouncing-ball videos that fill TikTok, Reels and Shorts. Pick a mode, change a few settings and watch it play. When the clip is ready, record it and download it. An idea becomes a video in a couple of minutes.
About.toolP2: The format works because it is simple. A ball bounces inside a ring with a gap. Every time it slips through, something pays off. Viewers want to know how it ends, so they keep watching.
About.tweakP: Add rings for a longer build-up or remove them for a fast payoff. Turn on rainbow walls, pick a break effect, add glow and a colour trail. Put your own image on the ball, write a hook across the top and load a melody. One extra ring can be the difference between a skip and a rewatch.
About.exportP: When the run looks right, record it in the browser and export a vertical video. No screen capture, no re-encoding. Save the setup as a preset and post a new one every day.

Vortex.canvasTitleFunnel: why marbles speed up in a funnel
Vortex.canvasSubtitleFunnel: falling in, a marble keeps its spin, / so every tighter circle is a faster lap
Vortex.vxFunnelDesc: Release the marbles as rings – waves of 6, 12 and 24, evenly spaced on the rim – and watch each ring spin up as it slips down the funnel: it keeps its spin while friction lets it sink, so every tighter circle is a faster lap. Seen from above or in perspective.
Vortex.vxPresetTip: Ring of 24: the loop clip – waves of 6, 12 and 24 every 4.5 s, in perspective at 25°. Galaxy: one ring of 360 seen from above. Coin funnel: one marble taking about a minute down a funnel with a small hole. Doubling: 1, 2, 4 … 256, with the lap readout. Each turns the refill loop on and sets the clip's navy page and loop HUD.
Vortex.vxReleaseTip: One by one: the balls enter one after another (the Sound Vortex, its ring notes and pews). Ring waves: waves of marbles released together, evenly spaced on the rim with the same speed and spin, so each wave stays a perfect ring all the way down; a lap of a ring plays a chime that rises as it spins up.
Vortex.vxViewTip: From above: the funnel seen straight down. Perspective: the funnel as a translucent bowl seen from the camera elevation, its spout narrowing to the hole, the marbles as glossy spheres in front of and behind each other.
Vortex.vxWavesTip: The marbles of each wave, in order – "6, 12, 24" releases a ring of 6, then 12, then 24. Any whole numbers from 1 up; a run builds at most the engine's ball ceiling in all. ×2 adds a wave twice the last one, − drops the last.
Vortex.vxWavesDouble: Add a wave twice the last one
Vortex.vxWavesCeiling: A run builds at most {count} marbles: the waves past that are cut.
Vortex.vxWaveIntervalTip: Seconds between two waves. 0 releases them all at once.
Vortex.vxSpinFrictionTip: How fast friction bleeds a ring's spin (per second). It is what lets a marble slip lower: more friction, a quicker drop. At 0 the rings keep their spin exactly and orbit the rim for ever.
Vortex.vxFirstLapTip: Seconds the first lap of a ring takes on the rim. The lap rate climbs from there as the ring sinks – the deeper, the faster.
Vortex.vxHoleSizeTip: The hole the rings vanish into, as a share of the rim. A smaller hole means a deeper spout and a far faster last lap (the default 25 % gives about 11 times the first lap's rate).
Vortex.vxRefillGapTip: Seconds the funnel stays empty after the last ring vanishes, before the first wave comes back (with the loop on). A noise wash covers the last second.
Vortex.vxLapReadoutTip: Shows the newest ring's lap time ("lap 1.23 s") under the funnel, in the loop HUD's counter line.
Vortex.vxElevationTip: How far above the funnel the camera looks from, in degrees: 90 is straight down (the top view), 25 is the loop clip's view.
Vortex.vxFunnelDepthTip: How deep the drawn funnel is: 0 is flat, 1 the loop clip's gravity well. It changes the picture only – the rings' timing comes from the friction and the first lap.
Vortex.vxRingInfo: {marbles} marbles in {waves} waves · {descent} s from rim to hole · one loop: {cycle} s · laps from {first} s down to {last} s ({gain}× faster)
Vortex.vxRingInfoFrictionless: {marbles} marbles · without friction the rings keep their spin and orbit the rim for ever: there is no loop.

ViralBot.title: Clip planner

Desktop.title: {siteName} for Windows
Desktop.intro: Everything the simulator does in the browser, plus what a browser cannot. Your graphics card encodes the videos, a queue works through batches while you do something else, and an AI studio on your PC plans clips and writes captions, offline.
Desktop.setupBody: Installs for your user only, no administrator rights, with a Start menu entry. Updates itself.

Desktop.smartScreenTitle: A warning from Chrome or Windows?
Desktop.smartScreenBody: The installer is not code-signed yet, and neither is the portable EXE. Chrome may say the file is not commonly downloaded, and Windows SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”. Windows does not know the publisher yet.

features.gpu: GPU video. The fast export encodes on the graphics card, with H.264 and HEVC through NVENC, AMF or Quick Sync, and with AV1 on newer cards.
features.queue: Render queue. Seeds, share links or the clip planner's plan, in every resolution, frame rate and codec you pick, saved straight into a folder. Progress, cancel, retry and resume after a restart.
features.ai: AI studio. A local model, downloaded once, or your own cloud key plans clips, writes hooks, captions and hashtags, and changes settings on request.
features.library: Library. Every clip you rendered with its thumbnail, length and post text. Play, show in folder, re-render or delete.
features.postiz: Post through Postiz. Pro sends a Library clip to TikTok, Instagram and YouTube through your own Postiz account, and you approve every post on a card. The autopilot proposes posts, you approve them.

Desktop.privacyBody: Everything runs on your PC. The local AI works offline. A cloud key you enter is stored encrypted and only sent to the provider you chose. The app sends us no usage data. It goes online to check for updates, to buy, restore or renew your Pro licence, to download a model you asked for, and for the account and publishing features you use. The privacy policy lists each one.
Desktop.updateWaitRender: A render is running. Wait for the queue to finish, or quit the app and the update installs as it closes.
Desktop.appInstallPortable: Portable · new versions come from the Download page
Desktop.setupNote: Free to download and use. Videos made without Pro carry a small watermark. Pro costs {price} a month.
Desktop.setupLegal: By downloading you accept the <terms>Terms</terms>. The <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> says what the app sends and where.
Desktop.smartScreenVerify: Before you run it, check the file. In PowerShell, Get-FileHash followed by the file name prints its SHA-256, which must match the line for that file in the checksums, ignoring upper and lower case. You can also search for the SHA-256 on <virustotal>VirusTotal</virustotal>.
Desktop.smartScreenSteps: If the checks pass, choose Keep in Chrome, then More info and Run anyway in Windows.
Desktop.privacyNoticesFfmpeg: ffmpeg, which the app uses to encode videos, is licensed under the GNU GPL version 3. It is the unmodified gyan.dev essentials build of FFmpeg 6.1.1, runs as a separate program and comes with its licence text. Its source code is available from the build's publisher and from the FFmpeg project, and we send it on request. The app lists every third-party component under Help, Third-party licences.
Desktop.privacyNoticesOther: The app is also built on Electron, Chromium, node-llama-cpp and llama.cpp. The licence texts of ffmpeg, Electron, Chromium and node-llama-cpp are shipped with the app. AI models are separate downloads under their own licences, which the app shows before you download. The AI studio can run Llama 3.2. Built with Llama.
Desktop.privacyAudio: The built-in sounds are synthesised by us. The built-in melodies are public-domain tunes.

privacy.title: Payments
privacy.content: Pro is paid through Stripe for cards or NOWPayments for crypto, on the provider's own checkout page and under its own privacy policy. Your card or wallet details never reach us. Our billing server, which runs on Cloudflare, keeps your email, the plan and the provider's payment or subscription reference, so that it can issue, renew and restore your licence. The licence itself is a signed key stored in your browser. We keep these records for as long as your licence can be restored and accounting rules require.
privacy.renewals: When your licence is about to run out or has just run out, the site and the Windows app ask the billing server whether your card subscription renewed. They send your email and the receipt reference.

terms.title: Pro subscriptions
terms.content: Playing with the simulator and recording or exporting videos is free. Videos made without a Pro licence carry a watermark. Pro costs {monthly} a month or {yearly} a year in US dollars, and tax may be added at checkout. The checkout shows the total before you pay. Pro exports videos without the watermark and adds quick share to TikTok, Instagram and YouTube with your device's share sheet or a download. Card subscriptions renew automatically until you cancel them in Stripe's customer portal. A crypto payment buys a prepaid period of 30 or 365 days that does not renew. A licence stays valid until the end of the period paid for.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.content: Pro is a digital licence, delivered at once. After the payment the pricing page activates it in your browser and shows a receipt reference. With your email and that reference you can restore the licence on any other device or in the Windows app at any time. Nothing is shipped.

refunds.title: Cancellation and refunds
refunds.content: You can cancel a card subscription at any time with Manage subscription on the pricing page. It then runs to the end of the period you have paid for and does not renew. Any first payment, by card or by crypto, is refunded in full if you ask within 14 days of paying. Write to {email} with the email you paid with and the receipt reference. For a crypto refund we also need a wallet address to send it to. Refunds reach a card in 5 to 10 business days. Renewals are not refundable unless the law of your country gives you that right. If you live in the EU or the UK, you also have the legal right to withdraw within 14 days of a purchase, as the next section explains.

withdrawal.title: Right of withdrawal in the EU and the UK
withdrawal.content: If you are a consumer in the EU or the UK, you can withdraw from a Pro purchase within 14 days of the payment without giving a reason. Send us a clear statement by email to {email}. You can use the model form below. We refund within 14 days of your message, to the payment method you used, or to a wallet address you give us for a crypto payment. Pro starts at once at your request. If you used Pro before withdrawing, we may keep a share of the price in proportion to the days used. After the first period, the same rule applies to each renewal.
